errors.english: what need is there for gold, jewels, pearls, or lapis lazuli to honor the Bodhisattva Mahasattva Dharmodgata?
errors.why: The merchant's daughter offers him the gold, jewels, pearls, lapis etc. with which he is to honor Dharmodgata (abbreviated sūtra quotation); the English invents a rhetorical question dismissing them.

fix.find: what need is there for gold, jewels, pearls, or lapis lazuli to honor the Bodhisattva Mahasattva Dharmodgata?
fix.replace: [take] the gold, jewels, pearls, lapis lazuli and so on with which you are to honor the Bodhisattva Mahasattva Dharmodgata

errors.english: let alone for many such teachings
errors.why: The a fortiori runs the other way: if one should give up bodies for Ganges-sand eons for each teaching, what need to mention giving up a single one.

note: Readable abridged retelling of the Sadāprarudita episode, but the merchant's daughter's offer of gold is turned into its opposite.
Faithful rendering of the commentary on the Mahāyāna-as-Buddhavacana argument, including the patriarch lineage.

errors.english: Although meditative absorption (samadhi) is shown as the entry, and the entry is shown as meditative absorption
errors.why: སྙོམས་པར་འཇུག་པ here is samāpatti, meditative attainment, contrasted with samādhi, not a generic 'entry'.

note: Accurate overall; unmarked inline glosses clutter it and samāpatti is flattened to 'entry'.

errors.english: If a preceptor or an abbot has faults
errors.why: མཁན་པོ is the upādhyāya and གནས here the niśraya teacher (ācārya of dependence); rendering གནས as 'abbot' throughout misidentifies the roles.

fix.find: If a preceptor or an abbot has faults
fix.replace: If the preceptor (upādhyāya) or the teacher of dependence (niśraya) has faults

errors.english: should not stay with a preceptor and an abbot, or not stay.
errors.why: One under ten years since ordination must not live without a preceptor or niśraya teacher.

fix.find: should not stay with a preceptor and an abbot, or not stay.
fix.replace: should not live without a preceptor or a teacher of dependence."

errors.english: This means that the abbot does not only ask questions
errors.why: The niśraya teacher too performs these services, the only difference being that he need not ask permission.
ལྷག་མ is a saṅghāvaśeṣa offence; 'remainder' is a calque that hides the Vinaya category.

errors.english: causing them to abandon unpleasant places
errors.why: This is dispelling discontent (arati), not leaving unpleasant places.

note: Vinaya roles (upādhyāya vs niśraya teacher vs pupil) are confused throughout and the ten-year rule is garbled.

errors.english: This is not the case; if it were to possess parts
errors.why: དེ་ལྟ་མ་ཡིན་ཏེ here means 'otherwise' (if it were not partless), supporting the preceding point rather than rejecting it.

note: Sound rendering of the atom/shape argument; one connective misread and some unmarked inline glosses.

errors.english: When one does not leave the walking area
errors.why: The side opens by finishing the rule: except those in which creatures do not arise, the rest should be discarded; this is not translated.
These are newly ordained bhikṣus; 'novice' suggests śrāmaṇeras.

note: Good rendering of the mat rule close and the eviction-rule narrative, apart from the dropped opening clause.

errors.english: with the intention of expressing clarity
errors.why: གསལ་བ here is vyakti, the individual instances; the plural expresses the particulars.

fix.find: with the intention of expressing clarity
fix.replace: with the intention of expressing the individual instances (vyakti)

errors.english: If the support causes the destruction of staying by itself or through another
errors.why: It says: if the support causes the staying of what perishes (by itself or from another), not that it destroys staying.
མཚམས་སྦྱོར་བ is pratisandhi, rebirth-linking; the mental consciousness that links rebirth is the 'being'.

note: Follows the dense pañjikā roughly but several technical points (vyakti, pratisandhi, the support argument) are misread.

errors.english: The meaning of the word "oneself" is "nature."
errors.why: བདག་ཉིད glosses svayam as 'oneself / the proponent himself', not 'nature'.

note: Generally faithful treatment of pakṣābhāsa and the word svayam in the thesis definition.
Faithful rendering of the sequence of faith and the instruction to stabilise it.
Accurate on the right view / right resolve quotation and the vāsanā argument; sūtra title misrendered.
